# T009 — Backend Azure SDK dependency remediation

## Summary

On 2026-10-21, removed the critical `fast-xml-parser` finding from **both** npm locks without changing backend APIs or making Azure calls. The parser moved from 5.3.0 to **5.7.0**, the first version outside every parser advisory range returned by the current npm audit. The other findings remain open.

## Changes

- `package.json`, `backend/package.json`: pin the Azure SDK's transitive `fast-xml-parser` to 5.7.0 through an npm override in each independently installable package root. The backend override is essential: root overrides do not apply to `npm ci --prefix backend --workspaces=false`.
- `package-lock.json`, `backend/package-lock.json`: regenerated using npm (`npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts`, standalone backend install, and `npm update fast-xml-parser --workspace backend --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts`); no hand-written lock entries. The new parser has additional 5.7.0 dependencies; the root lock re-hoists it instead of retaining the old nested parser.
- No application code, webhook routes, callback handling, or Azure configuration changed.

## Decisions

`npm explain fast-xml-parser` at both root and backend before changes traced 5.3.0 through backend `@azure/storage-blob@12.29.1` → `@azure/core-xml@1.5.0` (`fast-xml-parser: ^5.0.7`). `npm view @azure/storage-blob@12.29.1 dependencies.@azure/core-xml` returned `^1.4.5`; `npm view @azure/core-xml@1.6.0 dependencies --json` returned `fast-xml-parser: ^5.5.9`. Upgrading either Azure parent alone does **not** enforce 5.7.0 (versions 5.5.9–5.6.0 still match the newest advisory), whereas the pinned 5.7.0 override satisfies the existing parent range without introducing an unnecessary SDK/API change. npm registry `npm view fast-xml-parser@5.7.0 version` confirmed this version exists; npm audit and the linked GitHub advisories were consulted on 2026-10-21. No suppression, forced audit fix, or major Azure upgrade.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| [GHSA-m7jm-9gc2-mpf2](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-m7jm-9gc2-mpf2), `<5.3.5` in v5 | Critical | fast-xml-parser | 5.3.0 → 5.7.0 | Same | Fixed; entity encoding/regex bypass |
| [GHSA-jmr7-xgp7-cmfj](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jmr7-xgp7-cmfj), `<5.3.6` in v5 | High | fast-xml-parser | 5.3.0 → 5.7.0 | Same | Fixed; entity expansion DoS |

Parser use is potentially reachable while parsing XML returned by blob storage; the HTTP ACS callback endpoint itself handles JSON, not client-supplied XML. No claim that an attacker controls blob service XML or that a particular parser option is exercised. The offline mock Azure tests characterize existing callbacks but cannot verify real Azure interoperability.

## Follow-ups and risks

The remaining 35 root and 11 backend audit package findings are **open**, not waived or accepted; shared dependencies occur in both lock scans and are not additive unique findings. Examples include backend `@azure/identity`/`@azure/msal-node` (moderate), `jws`/`ws` (high), speech SDK and `uuid` (moderate), backend watcher dependencies, and frontend build dependencies; subsequent T010/T011 own remaining batches. The standalone install and mocked tests do not prove deployed Blob/ACS interoperability or production callback behavior; an authorized isolated Azure sandbox check would be needed separately. No live Azure or production call was made. Raw scan JSON stays in ignored `.modernization-scratch/scan/`.
